data.title: Power Integrations Reports Inducement Grants under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4)
data.description:
Power Integrations () today announced that on November 15, 2026 (the Grant Date), it granted a total of 42,411 RSUs and 1,361 PSUs at target to a total of 15 employees who began their employment with Power Integrations in October 2026.

The inducement grants were issued pursuant to Power Integrations’ Amended and Restated 2025 Inducement Award Plan. One-fourth (1/4th) of the RSUs will vest on each of the first four anniversaries of the respective Grant Dates, subject to the recipient’s continued service through each applicable vesting date. The PSUs will vest based upon achievement of the Company’s performance metrics for 2026, as determined by the Talent and Compensation Committee of the Company’s Board of Directors, up to a maximum of 200% of the target number of PSUs, subject to continued service through December 31, 2026. The inducement grants are subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable RSU and PSU agreements and Power Integrations’ Amended and Restated 2025 Inducement Award Plan.

The inducement grants were approved by the Talent and Compensation Committee of Power Integrations’ Board of Directors, as required by Nasdaq Rule 5635(c)(4), and were granted as a material inducement to employment in accordance with Nasdaq Rule 5635(c)(4).

About Power Integrations

Power Integrations, Inc. is a leading innovator in semiconductor technologies for high-voltage power conversion. The company’s products are key building blocks in the clean-power ecosystem, enabling the generation of renewable energy as well as the efficient transmission, conversion, and consumption of power in applications ranging from milliwatts to megawatts in applications such as AI data centers, EVs, and high-voltage direct current infrastructure. For more information, please visit www.power.com.

data.title: Notice to attend the extraordinary general meeting in Sleep Cycle AB (publ)
data.description:
The shareholders in Sleep Cycle AB (publ), reg. no. 556614-7368 ("Sleep Cycle" or the "Company"), with its registered office in Gothenburg, are hereby given notice to attend the extraordinary general meeting to be held on Tuesday 22 December 2026 at 10:00 a.m. CET at the offices of Audiowell, Riddargatan 30, SE-114 57 Stockholm, Sweden. Registration for the meeting commences at 9:30 a.m. CET.

Right to participate in the extraordinary general meeting and notice of participation

Participation at the meeting venue

Shareholders wishing to attend the meeting venue in person or by proxy must:

(i) be entered in the share register kept by Euroclear Nordics AB relating to the circumstances on 14 December 2026; and

(ii) notify the Company of their participation no later than 16 December 2026 by post to Sleep Cycle AB (publ), "Extra bolagsstämma december 2026", Drakegatan 10, SE-412 50 Gothenburg, Sweden, or by e-mail to investor@sleepcycle.com. The notification shall include the shareholder's name, personal identification number or corporate registration number, address, telephone number and the number of any assistants (not more than two) as well as, where applicable, information about any proxy.

A shareholder represented by proxy shall issue a written and dated power of attorney for the proxy. Power of attorney forms are available on the Company's website, investors.sleepcycle.com. If the power of attorney is issued by a legal entity, a registration certificate or equivalent documents of authority shall be enclosed. To facilitate registration at the meeting, the power of attorney as well as the registration certificate or other documents of authority should be received by the Company at the above address no later than 16 December 2026.

Participation by postal voting

Shareholders wishing to participate in the meeting by postal voting must (i) be entered in the share register kept by Euroclear Nordics AB relating to the circumstances on 14 December 2026, and (ii) notify the Company of their participation no later than 16 December 2026 by casting their postal vote in accordance with the instructions below, so that the postal vote is received by Sleep Cycle no later than that day. Shareholders wishing to attend the meeting venue, in person or by proxy, must give notice thereof in accordance with what is set out under Participation at the meeting venue above. This means that a notification by postal vote only is not sufficient for those who wish to attend the meeting venue.

A special form shall be used for postal voting. The postal voting form is available on the Company's website, investors.sleepcycle.com. The completed and signed postal voting form may be sent by post to Sleep Cycle AB (publ), "Extra bolagsstämma december 2026", Drakegatan 10, SE-412 50 Gothenburg, Sweden, or by e-mail to investor@sleepcycle.com. The completed and signed form must be received by Sleep Cycle no later than 16 December 2026. The shareholder may not provide the postal vote with special instructions or conditions. If so, the entire postal vote is invalid. Further instructions and conditions are set out in the postal voting form.

If a shareholder submits a postal vote by proxy, a written and dated power of attorney shall be enclosed with the postal voting form. Power of attorney forms are available on the Company's website, investors.sleepcycle.com. If the shareholder is a legal entity, a registration certificate or equivalent documents of authority shall be enclosed with the form. If a shareholder has submitted a postal vote and thereafter attends the meeting in person or by proxy, the postal vote remains valid to the extent the shareholder does not participate in a vote during the meeting or otherwise revokes the submitted postal vote. If the shareholder chooses to participate in a vote during the meeting, the vote cast will replace the previously submitted postal vote on that item.

Nominee registered shares

To be entitled to participate in the meeting, shareholders who have their shares registered in the name of a nominee must, in addition to giving notice of participation, have their shares registered in their own name so that the shareholder is included in the preparation of the share register as of 14 December 2026. Such registration may be temporary (so-called voting rights registration) and is requested from the nominee in accordance with the nominee's routines at such time in advance as the nominee determines. Voting rights registrations made by the nominee no later than 16 December 2026 will be taken into account in the preparation of the share register.

Item 10. Resolution on (A) implementation of a long-term incentive programme for senior executives and key individuals (LTIP 1), (B) a directed issue of warrants of series 2027/2030:1 and (C) approval of transfer of warrants

The board of directors proposes that the extraordinary general meeting resolves on implementation of a long-term incentive programme for senior executives and key individuals in the form of a warrant programme ("LTIP 1") comprising (A) implementation of the incentive programme as set out below, (B) a directed issue of no more than 2,150,000 warrants of series 2027/2030:1 to the Company and/or any of its subsidiaries (the Company or a subsidiary, as applicable, hereinafter referred to as the "LTIP Company", and the group where the Company is the parent company, hereinafter referred to as the "Group") and (C) approval of transfer of warrants from the LTIP Company to the participants. LTIP 1 is complemented by LTIP 2 pursuant to item 11, which is directed to the same participants.

Background and rationale

The extraordinary general meeting held on 11 November 2026 resolved on an issue in kind of new shares in the Company as consideration for the acquisition of all shares in Audiowell AB from Audiowell Group AB. The acquisition is expected to be completed at the end of November 2026. The combination of Sleep Cycle and Audiowell marks a clearer strategic focus on the global wellness market and is the starting point for building a group of businesses addressing this market. The acquisition and the new strategic focus place high demands on management and key individuals, both in the integration of the businesses and in the work to realise the opportunities provided by the combined business. Against this background, the board of directors considers it particularly important to be able to retain and attract qualified employees and to create a long-term alignment of interests between them and the Company's shareholders.

The board of directors is of the opinion that share-related incentive programmes are an appropriate means of achieving this. LTIP 1 and LTIP 2 give senior executives and key individuals the opportunity, through their own investment on market terms, to share in the increase in value that they contribute to creating. Since the subscription prices correspond to 150 and 200 percent, respectively, of the Offer Price (as defined below), the programmes only provide an outcome upon a significant share price increase, which means that the outcome for the Participants (as defined below) is directly linked to the shareholders' return. The programmes are thereby expected to increase the Participants' commitment to, and long-term focus on, the development of the Group. The board of directors assesses that this is in line with the interests of all shareholders.

(A) Main terms of the incentive programme

Participants and allocation

LTIP 1 shall encompass the CEO, the Company's group management and other key individuals within the Group, including consultants to the Group and future recruits to corresponding positions (the "Participants"). Board members of the Company will not be allowed to participate. LTIP 1 is expected to comprise around 32 Participants. The Participants are offered, after having entered into an agreement with the LTIP Company, to acquire warrants at market value. The Participants' right to warrants shall be differentiated based on position, responsibility and work performance in the Group. The Participants are divided into the categories below. Only persons in the mentioned categories, or new recruits with similar positions and responsibility, shall be offered warrants. The board of directors shall have the right to decide on the persons to be included in the different categories in accordance with the guidelines set out in this item and the overall intention of LTIP 1.

Total2,150,000

Allocation shall take place after the publication of the Company's year-end report for 2026 and no later than 30 April 2027. The board of directors shall be entitled to extend the allocation period. Warrants that are not transferred to Participants shall be cancelled.

Warrant Agreement and vesting

A prerequisite for receiving warrants is that the Participant enters into an agreement with the LTIP Company (the "Warrant Agreement"). The Warrant Agreement will include a so-called vesting structure, a repurchase right for the LTIP Company applicable under certain circumstances, certain transfer restrictions and other terms and conditions customary for such agreements, with some potential differences due to requirements under local law.

The vesting structure is to be implemented by way of transferring all warrants to the respective Participant upfront, subject to a reversed vesting mechanism with a contractual obligation to transfer all or part of the warrants back to the Group. Under the reversed vesting schedule, 1/3 of the warrants will vest at the end of each of the three years following allocation, until the three-year vesting period is over.

Subscription price and term

Each warrant shall entitle the warrant holder to subscribe for one (1) new share in the Company. The subscription price per new share shall be fixed and amount to SEK 36.75, corresponding to 150 percent of the offer price of SEK 24.50 per share in Snark BidCo AB's public takeover offer to the shareholders of the Company (the "Offer Price"), which also corresponds to the issue price in the issue in kind in connection with the acquisition of Audiowell AB. The warrants may be exercised for subscription of new shares during the period from and including 15 May 2030 until and including 15 June 2030. Subscription of new shares may however not take place during so-called closed periods according to the EU Market Abuse Regulation or otherwise in breach of applicable insider rules.

Support for participation

The LTIP Company or another company in the Group shall be allowed to support participation by offering Participants in the categories group management and other key individuals a cash compensation (bonus) corresponding to no more than 50 percent of the amount, net of tax, that the Participant shall pay for the warrants. However, the Company's aggregate cost for the cash compensation shall be capped at the cost arising at a share price corresponding to the Offer Price, and the cash compensation may therefore be lower than 50 percent if the market value of the warrants at the time of transfer is higher. The CEO will not receive any such subsidy, but will acquire the warrants at full market value. The cash compensation shall be paid in connection with the acquisition of the warrants and will be taxable in accordance with applicable tax regulations. The cash compensation is resolved upon by the general meeting as part of LTIP 1 and LTIP 2 and is therefore not covered by the Company's guidelines for remuneration to senior executives.

Preparation of the proposal

This proposal has been prepared by the board of directors together with external advisors. The final proposal has been presented by the board of directors.

Dilution

Upon full subscription, transfer and exercise of all 2,150,000 warrants, 2,150,000 new shares will be issued and the share capital will increase by no more than SEK 59,722.22. This corresponds to a dilution of approximately 1.88 percent of the total number of shares and votes in the Company, calculated as the number of new shares in relation to the sum of existing and new shares, based on the 112,319,775 shares that will be outstanding in the Company following registration of the issue in kind to Audiowell Group AB. Together with LTIP 2 pursuant to item 11, LTIP 3 pursuant to item 12 and LTIP 4 pursuant to item 13, the aggregate dilution amounts to no more than 3.44 percent, calculated on the same basis. The dilution calculation does not take into account any new shares as a result of existing incentive programmes.

Scope and costs of the programme

The warrants are transferred at market value, and therefore no costs under IFRS 2 are expected to arise for the Company as a result of the transfer as such. The market value has been preliminarily calculated by an independent valuation firm at SEK 4.37 per warrant using the Black & Scholes valuation model, based on a share price corresponding to the Offer Price of SEK 24.50, the subscription price of SEK 36.75, a term of three years, a volatility of 42 percent and a risk-free interest rate of 2.75 percent. The Company's costs for the subsidy, including social security contributions, are estimated at no more than approximately SEK 9.3 million, corresponding to the cost at a share price equal to the Offer Price. Since the cost is capped at this amount, the cost of the subsidy will not be higher at a higher share price at the time of transfer, but may be lower at a lower share price. In addition, there will be costs for valuation, advisory services, registration and administration.

Quotient exercise model

To reduce the investment cost for the Participants in connection with the exercise of the warrants, as well as the dilution for the shareholders, the board of directors shall be entitled, but not obliged, to allow subscription of new shares to be made by application of the quotient exercise model set out in the complete terms and conditions for the warrants. Pursuant to the quotient exercise model, only the quotient value is paid for new shares (currently approximately SEK 0.027778 per share), while the number of new shares that the warrants entitle to subscription of is reduced so that the Participants will have the same financial upside, but a lower number of shares, as if each warrant had entitled to subscription of one (1) new share at the subscription price. The quotient exercise model shall not be applied if the formula entails a right to subscription of a negative number of shares, in which case each warrant shall entitle to subscription of one (1) new share, subject to any adjustments in accordance with the complete terms and conditions. If the quotient exercise model is applied, the actual dilution and share capital increase will be lower than set out above.

Existing share-related incentive programmes

As of the date of this notice, the Company has two outstanding share-related incentive programmes, both in the form of warrant programmes: Warrant programme 2023/2027 (CEO LTIP), which was resolved upon at the extraordinary general meeting held on 23 November 2023 and is directed to the Company's CEO, and Warrant programme 2024/2027, which was resolved upon at the annual general meeting held on 11 April 2024 and is directed to employees of the Company. All warrants in the respective programmes have been subscribed for and transferred at market value calculated using the Black & Scholes valuation model. The table below sets out the total number of warrants outstanding as of the date of this notice as well as the number of new shares in the Company in the event the warrants are exercised.

2023/2027 (CEO LTIP)100,000SEK 52.601 December 2026 – 2 January 2027

The reason for the deviation from the shareholders' preferential rights is that the warrants are to be used within LTIP 1.
  • Subscription of warrants shall be made on a separate subscription list no later than 30 April 2027. The board of directors shall be entitled to extend the subscription period. The Company is not to pay any subscription price for the warrants. Any subsidiary subscribing for warrants shall pay a subscription price corresponding to the market value of the warrants, calculated by an independent valuation firm engaged by the Company using the Black & Scholes valuation model. In such case, payment shall be made in connection with subscription and no later than 30 April 2027. The board of directors shall be entitled to extend the period for payment.
  • Each warrant entitles to subscription of one (1) new share in the Company at a subscription price of SEK 36.75 during the period from and including 15 May 2030 until and including 15 June 2030. Warrants that have not been exercised for subscription of new shares by 15 June 2030 at the latest shall lapse. The subscription price and the number of shares that each warrant entitles to may be subject to recalculation in accordance with customary recalculation terms and the quotient exercise model set out in the complete terms and conditions for the warrants. The subscription price may never be below the quotient value of the share.
  • The warrants shall otherwise be subject to the complete terms and conditions set out in the complete proposal. The board of directors, the CEO or a person appointed by the board of directors shall be authorised to make any minor adjustments to the resolution that may be required in connection with registration with the Swedish Companies Registration Office.

(C) Approval of transfer of warrants

It is proposed that the general meeting approves that the LTIP Company transfers warrants of series 2027/2030:1 to the Participants in accordance with (A) above. Transfer shall be made against cash payment corresponding to the market value of the warrants at the time of transfer, calculated by an independent valuation firm using the Black & Scholes valuation model. The market value is preliminarily estimated at SEK 4.37 per warrant.

Majority requirements

The proposal is subject to the provisions of Chapter 16 of the Swedish Companies Act (Sw. aktiebolagslagen (2005:551)), and a valid resolution therefore requires that the proposal is supported by shareholders representing at least nine-tenths (9/10) of the votes cast as well as of the shares represented at the general meeting.

data.title: Clean-Energy Investors Look Beyond Carbon Emissions — Market Talk
data.description: Private-market investors looking to capitalize on the economy's transition to clean energy favor strategies aimed at boosting the security and resilience of energy sources, rather than just reducing carbon emissions, according to Australian infrastructure specialist IFM Investors. "For investors, it is no longer enough for energy to be renewable; it must also be resilient," IFM says in a report. As an example, it cites Australia's power market, where abundant solar sources often lead to negative wholesale electricity prices. "Standalone solar is less compelling for institutional investors," IFM says. "Solar power paired with battery storage, however, is a different proposition." In Europe, too, investors' appetite for renewables varies with markets and technologies, IFM says. "We see growth in transmission, onshore wind and battery storage, but less attractive returns in offshore wind." (luis.garcia@wsj.com; @lhvgarcia)

Trump weighs fresh Iran strikes as Centcom warns of force strain - report
data.description:
President Donald Trump is facing growing pressure from hawkish U.S. officials and Israeli leaders to restart joint military strikes on Iran, as U.S. Central Command warns that a sustained deployment beyond December threatens to erode military readiness, according to a media report published Friday.

Centcom has briefed administration officials that the toll on forces from maintaining the military build-up past year-end could compromise readiness, the Financial Times reported, citing three people familiar with the matter, including U.S. officials.

One source told the FT that Centcom is telling the administration it is "running out of time, burning money and readiness," including the capacity to address other global threats, with the large deployment against Iran nearing a full year.

Military planners are also eyeing an incoming Democratic-led Congress likely to curtail defense spending and tighten oversight of the war. A U.S. military official disputed the characterization, the FT reported, saying it was not true that Centcom was warning forces would become overextended if strikes were not renewed before the new year.

Israeli officials have seized on the shrinking window argument. Caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu—serving after an inconclusive election—has warned repeatedly of "great threats" from Iran and claimed without evidence that Tehran is pushing to restart its nuclear program,the FT reported. Mossad chief Roman Gofman traveled to Washington last week for talks with CIA Director John Ratcliffe in a bid to "provide information and persuade" the Trump administration to renew joint strikes. Israel's security establishment is also reportedly discussing a smaller operation if broad joint action fails to materialize.

Trump, however, has appeared reluctant to commit, telling Axios on Thursday he was not "rushing into any decision" and would "see what happens after the beginning of the year." The president has oscillated between threats and calls for diplomacy, more recently saying he is content with the status quo—a naval blockade on Iran.

data.title: Ford, Honda, Stellantis, VW sue New Jersey to block 'extortionate' vehicle repair law
data.description:
By Jonathan Stempel

Ford , Honda , Stellantis' FCA unit and Volkswagen sued New Jersey on Friday to block a new state law they say increases the amounts automakers must pay franchised dealers for warranty and recall repairs.

In a complaint filed in federal court in Trenton, New Jersey, the automakers said the New Jersey Motor Vehicle Open Recall Notice and Fair Compensation Act gives dealers a "blank check" to set prices for warranty, recall and other repair services, while prohibiting manufacturers from avoiding "extortionate" results or recovering the costs.

New Jersey's law will shift more than $375 million a year to dealers from automakers, giving dealers a "windfall" by imposing no obligation to use the money to improve customer service or boost compensation for employees, the automakers said.

"In short, the act rewards dealers for charging their customers more," the automakers said.

The office of New Jersey Attorney General Jennifer Davenport, who enforces the state's laws, did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

New Jersey's law took effect on April 1, after former Governor Phil Murphy signed it in September 2025.

CONSTITUTIONAL VIOLATIONS ALLEGED

The automakers objected to letting dealers charge a "labor multiplier" based on samples of repair orders, saying it lets dealers bill for substantially more labor time than they actually work.

They also challenged provisions requiring automakers to pay marked-up prices on parts that the dealers received at reduced cost or for free, and preventing automakers from providing less expensive parts even if supply, demand or other factors justified price cuts.

Ford, Honda, FCA — which includes Fiat and Chrysler — and Volkswagen said that since the law took effect, each has received dozens of bills requiring payment "for hours that no technician works, that surpass what comparable dealers charge for the same work, and that exceed what retail customers pay."

They said the law violates the US Constitution's Commerce Clause and Takings Clause, is preempted by federal law governing recalls, and violates New Jersey's Constitution.

The nonprofit New Jersey Coalition of Automotive Retailers is also a defendant. It did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

data.title: Cattle Futures Rise Ahead of Feedlot Report — Market Talk
data.description: Live cattle futures rose for a third consecutive session as the market awaited the USDA's monthly Cattle on Feed report. Cattle and calves on feed totaled 11.6 million head as of Nov. 1, down 1% from a year before. Placements on feedlots in October fell 7% from the year-earlier month to 1.89 million head, the lowest for the month on records back to 1996. Marketings of fed cattle at 1.62 million head were also a record low for October, and down 5% on the year. "Monthly Cattle on Feed reports have repeatedly shown tighter than expected supply in recent months, but the subsequent optimism has typically not lasted long with heavy selling pressure clouding not just the cattle complex, but broader livestock/protein sector as a whole," Mike Castle of StoneX says in a note. Live cattle settled up 0.1% on CME at $2.23 a pound ahead of the report. Hogs edge up 0.3% to 52.6 cents a pound. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
